title: Go-To-Market Canvas
subtitle: You're about to launch a new product, enter a new market, or take a new offer to existing
useWhen: customers and you don't have a structured plan. You're moving fast but not strategically. Things will fall through the cracks.
howToUse: A Go-To-Market (GTM) Canvas is a structured plan that maps seven elements of a successful launch: Target Segment (who exactly), Value Proposition (why this, why now), Channels (how you reach them), Pricing (how you charge), Sales Motion (how you convert), Success Metrics (how you know it's working), and Launch Timeline (sequenced actions). Without a GTM Canvas, launches become activity without direction, lots of effort, unclear results.
steps: Complete the Target Segment and Value Proposition first, everything else follows from those.
Define success metrics before launch, not after. What number will tell you this worked?
Map the Sales Motion specifically, who does what, in what order, using which assets.

Set a 30-day, 60-day, and 90-day milestone to know whether to accelerate or adjust. Plan your launch so it lands, not just ships If Target Segment or Value Proposition is wrong, the other five elements just execute the mistake faster and more efficiently.
origin: VC & startup GTM methodology — widely documented in startup literature
promptBody:
Act as a go-to-market strategist.
What I am launching  :   [PRODUCT, SERVICE, OR NEW MARKET ENTRY]
Launch date target      :  [WHEN YOU WANT TO GO LIVE]
Resources available     :  [TEAM SIZE, BUDGET RANGE, CHANNELS]
Build a complete GTM Canvas:
TARGET SEGMENT     :  Who specifically - ICP description
VALUE PROP                :  Why this, why now, why us
CHANNELS                   :  How we reach them - ranked by priority
PRICING                        :  Model and rationale
SALES MOTION           :  Steps from awareness to closed deal
SUCCESS METRICS    :  The 3 numbers that define success
TIMELINE                     :  Key milestones for weeks 1, 2, 4, 8
Flag the highest-risk assumption in this GTM plan and suggest how to validate it before
full launch.

proTip:
The highest-risk GTM assumption is almost always Channel, not product. Most founders
assume a channel will work before testing it. Before investing in a full launch, run a 2-
week channel test with minimal spend. Let data pick your primary channel, not your
preference.
